what_office_does.text: The superintendent is an independently elected, nonpartisan voice for the public in California’s education systems. The office advocates with the Legislature and governor and serves on governing boards from transitional kindergarten through higher education.
what_office_does.label: fact

candidates.name: Richard Barrera

says.text: Barrera says he would bring San Diego Unified’s school reforms statewide to improve student success.
says.label: value

says.text: Barrera says he brought parents, educators, and the community together to cut bureaucracy and invest in students and classrooms.
says.label: fact

says.text: Barrera says he worked to keep ICE out of schools, support LGBTQ students, and ensure children were vaccinated.
says.label: fact

candidates.headline: Barrera says he would bring San Diego Unified’s reforms statewide to improve student success.
candidates.core_case: Barrera presents his school board experience as a model for improving schools statewide. He says bringing families and educators together helped direct money to classrooms and improve reading, math, and readiness for college and careers.
priorities: Investing in students and the classroom

candidates.name: Sonja Shaw

says.text: Shaw says she would restore high academic standards in reading, writing, and math across California’s public schools.
says.label: value

says.text: Shaw says she would cut bureaucracy and require financial transparency so school funding reaches classrooms and supports students and teachers.
says.label: value

says.text: Shaw says she would protect Title IX, emphasizing fairness in girls’ sports and safety and privacy in girls’ spaces.
says.label: value

candidates.headline: Shaw says she would restore high academic standards in reading, writing, and math statewide.
candidates.core_case: Shaw presents her school board leadership as a model for improving schools statewide. She says focusing on basic academics, directing resources to classrooms, and involving parents improved student outcomes in her district.

where_they_differ.text: Both emphasize academics and classroom resources. Barrera highlights expanding San Diego’s reforms and his work on immigrant and LGBTQ student protections, while Shaw emphasizes basic academic standards, financial transparency, and protections for girls’ sports and private spaces.
